questions.question: What are vision-language models (VLMs) capable of processing?
options: Only text inputs with image descriptions
Both text and image inputs, enabling tasks like document extraction and chart analysis
Only images without any text context
Video streams in real-time
questions.explanation: VLMs like GPT-4o and Gemini 1.5 Pro accept both text and image inputs. This enables document intelligence (invoice extraction, contract analysis), chart interpretation, and multi-page PDF processing — unlocking the 80% of enterprise data that isn't plain text.

questions.question: What is the recommended approach for processing a 50-page PDF with a VLM?
options: Send the entire PDF as a single API call
Convert each page to an image, process per page, then synthesize results
Use OCR only — VLMs can't handle PDFs
Split the PDF into 5-page chunks and process each as text
questions.explanation: The recommended approach is to convert each page to an image, extract structured data per page using the VLM, then synthesize the per-page results. This handles complex layouts, tables, and mixed content that text extraction would miss.

questions.question: When should you use OCR-first processing instead of VLM-based extraction?
options: When documents contain handwriting
When processing high volumes of standardized documents at lower cost
When accuracy is the top priority
When documents contain tables
questions.explanation: OCR-first (AWS Textract, Azure Document Intelligence) is more cost-effective for high-volume standardized documents. VLMs are better for complex layouts, handwritten annotations, and documents requiring semantic understanding — but at higher per-page cost.

questions.question: What is the 'detail' parameter when sending images to GPT-4o?
options: The resolution of the generated image output
A setting that controls how many tokens the model uses to analyze the image (low vs high)
The compression quality of the uploaded image
The level of explanation in the text response
questions.explanation: The 'detail' parameter controls analysis depth: 'low' uses fewer tokens (cheaper, faster) for simple images, while 'high' uses more tokens for detailed analysis of complex documents with small text or intricate layouts.

questions.question: What percentage of enterprise data is estimated to be non-plain-text (images, PDFs, scanned docs)?
options: About 20%
About 40%
About 60%
About 80%
questions.explanation: Approximately 80% of enterprise data exists in unstructured formats — scanned documents, PDFs, images, handwritten notes, and presentations. VLMs are transformative because they unlock this previously inaccessible data for AI-powered analysis.
